Title: Wawasan: Najib's conditional pardon must be respected by all parties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) has welcomed the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, saying the decision by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, should be respected by all parties.
Wawasan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah said the decision had brought an end to the controversy surrounding Najib's pardon and expressed appreciation to Sultan Ibrahim for resolving the matter.
"The Article 42(1) of the Federal Constitution provided the King with the power to grant pardons, reprieves and respites.
"This is the prerogative and power of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, and all parties should respect it," he said in a statement.
He said the party also conveyed its appreciation to the King for His Majesty's wisdom in bringing the issue to a conclusion.
Najib was granted
a conditional pardon
allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house detention until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
Saifuddin said the constitutional provision should be respected regardless of political affiliation, stressing that the King's prerogative was provided for under the Federal Constitution.

Title: Nearly 1 in 4 doctors worldwide approaching retirement age
Article:
GENEVA: Nearly one in four doctors worldwide is over the age of 55 and is expected to retire within the next decade, the World Health Organisation (WHO) warned Friday, highlighting growing pressure on health systems, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
The finding, based on the latest available data from 122 countries, was published in WHO's new report on global health workforce levels and trends. In high-income countries, nearly one in three doctors is approaching retirement age.
"Ageing is the hidden health workforce crisis that requires urgent attention," said Khassoum Diallo, acting head of WHO's health workforce policies and data unit.
WHO projects a global shortage of 11.1 million health workers by 2030, with 67 countries expected to lack enough personnel to meet their populations' health needs.
Despite the challenges, global health workforce density rose 52 per cent over the past two decades, from 44.8 workers per 10,000 people in 2006 to 67.9 in 2025, according to the report. More than 70 million health and care workers are now employed worldwide.
Large regional disparities persist, however. WHO said doctor density in Europe is 13 times higher than in Africa, while nurse and midwife density is six times higher.
"Addressing these inequities is essential to achieving Health for All," Diallo said.

Title: PH: No one above law, convicted offenders must serve sentences
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council today stressed that no one is above the law and that anyone convicted of an offence must serve their sentence in accordance with the Federal Constitution and the law.
In a statement issued after its meeting today, the council said it stood firmly behind Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's position, as well as the advice given by the Attorney-General and Federal Territories Minister to the Pardons Board.
"The PH Presidential Council firmly stands with the position of the prime minister, as well as the advice given by the Attorney-General and the Federal Territories Minister to the Pardons Board today," it said.
The council said no individual was above the law and that those convicted must undergo their punishment in accordance with the provisions of the Federal Constitution.
It said the principle of equality before the law remained fundamental and should be upheld in matters involving criminal convictions and punishment.
The council also reaffirmed its commitment to combating corruption, advancing the Reformasi agenda and cleaning up the country from corruption and misappropriation.
"The council is determined to continue efforts to combat corruption, uphold the Reform agenda and cleanse the country of elements of corruption and misappropriation," it said.
The statement was issued following the PH Presidential Council meeting, which began at about 5.30pm and ended after nearly two hours at the Perdana Putra complex.
The meeting comes amid renewed political attention following the decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under conditional house arrest, subject to a RM50 million fine.
Najib was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
The decision has also reignited political discussion within Umno, with analysts saying it could revive the "Bossku" sentiment among sections of the party's grassroots and increase pressure on Umno to be more vocal in defending its former president.
The PH meeting also follows remarks by BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at the 2026 Umno general assembly last week, when he challenged those calling for the party to end its cooperation with the unity government.
Zahid said those seeking to end the cooperation should either call for the dissolution of Parliament to pave the way for the 16th general election (GE16), or table a motion of no confidence against the government in the Dewan Rakyat.
His remarks have since fuelled renewed discussion over BN's position in the unity government and the future of the coalition.
On Monday, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke called on Anwar to convene the PH Presidential Council meeting immediately to discuss recent political developments.
Loke said the meeting should be held as soon as Anwar returned from his official overseas visit, citing several political statements made recently which he described as detrimental to political certainty and stability in the country.

Title: Perak, Melaka, Johor Umno back Najib solidarity fund
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno leaders in Perak, Melaka and Johor have welcomed the party's initiative to raise funds to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak settle his RM50 million fine.
Perak Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the state chapter was grateful for the Pardons Board's decision to grant Najib a conditional pardon.
Saarani who is also Perak menteri besar also expressed his appreciation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia for granting the pardon.
"The judicial process is respected and implemented, while the pardoning power vested in the Yang di-Pertuan Agong is a symbol of wisdom and compassion within the constitutional monarchy system that we uphold," he said in a statement.
Saarani said the development would bring relief to Najib and his family and be welcomed with gratitude by Umno members nationwide.
He also welcomed Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's initiative to launch a contribution fund to help Najib settle the RM50 million fine.
"Perak Umno is ready to work together to make the initiative a success as a sign of togetherness and solidarity with Datuk Seri Najib," he said.
Meanwhile, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh urged Najib's supporters to use various means to raise funds to help the former prime minister settle the fine.
"I urge those who love Datuk Najib to use various means to raise funds to help settle the fine," he said to reporters at the Tanjung Bidara state constituency.
In Johor, Umno info chief Md Israk Abdullah said Najib's house arrest is not a release or cancellation of the conviction.
"Datuk Seri Najib is still serving the remainder of his sentence based on the terms decided through legitimate channels," he said in a statement.
Md Israk also urged all parties to respect the decision and not distort the facts for political interests.
"The principle of the rule of law must be respected consistently and cannot be practised selectively," he said.
He also backed Umno Malaysia's Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, saying those wishing to contribute voluntarily towards helping Najib settle the fine could do so through the fund.
Earlier, Umno announced the
nationwide fund
following the conditional pardon granted to Najib, which allows him to serve
the remainder of his sentence
under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine.

Title: Ringgit ends higher against greenback on easing oil supply concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar and other major currencies at Friday's close, buoyed by improved market sentiment following easing concerns over crude oil supply, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the local currency rose to 4.0795/0840 versus the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0965/1010.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude prices fell on expectations of improving conditions in the Strait of Hormuz.
"This followed Saudi Arabia's move to restore the damaged East-West pipeline. At the same time, some tankers have continued to traverse the Straits of Hormuz," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit gained against the euro to 4.6849/6901 from Thursday's close of 4.7003/7055, rose versus the Japanese yen to 2.5829/5860 from 2.6305/6336 yesterday, and advanced vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4543/4603 from 5.4877/4937 previously.
The local note also traded higher against its Asean peers.
The ringgit inched up versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1933/1971 from 3.2099/2137 at yesterday's close and improved against the Thai baht to 12.2383/2562 from 12.2734/2917 previously.
It also appreciated vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.53/6.54 yesterday and climbed versus the Indonesian rupiah to 229.7/230.0 from 230.7/231.1.

Title: ES Sunlogy wins Parkland Southern contract in Johor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ES Sunlogy Bhd's wholly-owned Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd has secured a RM15.6 million contract from Parkland Southern Sdn Bhd for electrical works at a development in Johor.
The contract involves the supply, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning and maintenance of electrical, telephone and extra-low-voltage services for the second phase of a development along Johor Bahru-Pasir Gudang Highway.
The development comprises two 29-storey serviced apartment towers as well as a seven-storey podium featuring serviced apartments, recreational facilities, parking facilities and commercial space.
Savelite will enter into a nominated sub-contract with TSB Builders Sdn Bhd, the main contractor, under the conditions outlined in Pertubuhan Akitek Malaysia (PAM) Sub-Contract 2006.
The commencement and completion dates will follow the main contractor's schedule.
ES Sunlogy's share price closed unchanged at 42 sen on Friday, valuing the company at RM316.15 million.

Title: Carimin raises Sealink stake to 24.1pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Carimin Petroleum Bhd has increased its direct stake in Sealink International Bhd to 24.1 per cent.
This followed the acquisition of 23 million Sealink shares via a direct business transaction.
A Bursa Malaysia filing dated Sept 18 showed that Carimin's direct holdings rose to 120.5 million shares from 97.5 million previously.
The acquisition comes after Carimin's proposed RM165 million privatisation of Sealink lapsed following opposition from a major shareholder.
Carimin had previously said it intended to raise its stake in Sealink to as much as 32.5 per cent, at a maximum price of 41 sen per share, subject to takeover rules.

Title: Macau concludes first closed-door national security trial
Article:
MACAU: Macau has concluded its first national security trial behind closed doors, a court said on Friday, days after proceedings began in a former pro-democracy lawmaker's case.
A verdict will be issued at a later date, Macau's Court of First Instance said in a statement.
The Chinese casino hub expanded the scope of national security laws in May 2023, and a bill passed this year allows judges to hear national security cases behind closed doors.
Au Kam San, a former Macau lawmaker who was detained in July 2025 on charges including subversion, was the first person to be arrested under the island's new laws and the first to face a closed trial.
The proceedings, which opened on Wednesday, have ended, the Court of First Instance said, adding that "the verdict will be delivered on a date to be scheduled later."
It said that Au, who was charged with "subversion of state power" as well as building ties with foreign groups and media outlets deemed harmful to China, "is accused of endangering national security."
Michael Polak, a London-based barrister representing 69-year-old Au, criticised the handling of the case.
"The fact that the 'trial' of Mr Au was completed... in secret, without him being represented by independent counsel underlines the farcical nature of the proceedings," Polak told AFP.
It is "impossible for evidence to have been properly evaluated and a proper process to have been followed for such a serious offence in such a short period of time," he said.
The closed-door trial, "shielded from public and press scrutiny, because secrecy conceals miscarriages of justice", said Jorge Menezes, a Portuguese lawyer who has practised in Macau.
"It is not about justice, security, or the rule of law; it is designed to intimidate everyone into submission to the Chinese Communist Party," Menezes told AFP before the trial.
Au was one of the organisers of annual vigils in Macau – a former Portuguese territory which reverted to China in 1999 – in memory of the victims of the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown.
Macau and Hong Kong were once the only places in China where such public commemorations could take place.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Australia move towards strategic defence collaboration - Khaled
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Australia have agreed to elevate their existing defence ties from cooperation to closer, more practical and strategic collaboration, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
He said the agreement was reached at the sixth Malaysia-Australia High-Level Committee (HLC) Meeting, which he co-chaired with Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles in Geelong, Australia today.
Khaled said the Strategic Planning Committee (SPC) would serve as a key mechanism to ensure that every agreed initiative had clear direction and follow-up action.
"This includes initiatives in technology as well as defence capability development for both countries.
"This is the direction of Malaysia-Australia defence relations, moving from cooperation to collaboration and subsequently building stronger togetherness in facing future security challenges," he said in a post on his official Facebook page.
Earlier, Khaled and Marles held a bilateral meeting before co-chairing the HLC meeting.
The sixth HLC meeting marked the culmination of Khaled's three-day working visit to Australia to assess progress in defence cooperation and chart the future direction of bilateral defence relations.
The meeting followed the fifth HLC session held in Kuala Lumpur on Aug 21, 2025, with this year's meeting also focusing on exploring new opportunities for defence cooperation between Malaysia and Australia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang Sultan witnesses signing of wind turbine project agreement in Pekan
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah Al-Sultan Abdullah, witnessed the signing ceremony of a collaboration agreement to develop a wind turbine project in Pekan.
The agreement was signed between Amat Bayu Sdn Bhd, a member of the Tadau Group, and representatives from the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
Amat Bayu director Datuk Ahmad Najmi Abdul Razak, who signed the agreement on behalf of the company, said the event marked an important milestone for Amat Bayu and its UAE partners in developing the 2.2-megawatt wind turbine project in Tanjung Batu, Pekan.
"This project is beyond the development of a single wind turbine, it is about taking the first step towards unlocking the potential of wind energy in Malaysia.
"We are particularly proud that this journey begins here in Pahang, which will serve as an important platform to build local experience, generate valuable data and, ultimately, provide a stronger foundation for larger-scale wind energy development in Malaysia," he said in his speech.
Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and UAE Ambassador to Malaysia Mubarak Saeed Ahmed Burshaid Al Dhaheri.

Title: Jati Tinggi Group lands RM72.8mil data centre job, order book swells to RM1.1bil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jati Tinggi Group Bhd's wholly-owned Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd has secured a RM72.8 million contract for power infrastructure works linked to a data centre in Banting, Selangor.
The contract covers the design, supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of a 275kV cable connection for a data centre at Banting Technology Park.
The project is scheduled for completion by Jan 15 next year, Tinggi Group said in a statement today.
Following the latest award, Tinggi Group's outstanding order book has risen to about RM1.1 billion, providing earnings visibility for the next three years.
Contract wins for the year-to-date financial year 2026 have reached RM544.6 million, already exceeding the RM460.4 million secured for the whole of FY25.
Managing director Datuk Wira Lim Yeong Seong said the latest award reflected growing opportunities in private-sector power infrastructure, particularly as data centres drive demand for medium- and high-voltage connections.
"With our order book now standing at about RM1.1 billion, we are encouraged by the growing diversity of our project portfolio," he said.
Lim said the company's capabilities across multiple voltage levels would allow it to participate in a wider range of power infrastructure projects, alongside its existing projects linked to Tenaga Nasional Bhd.

Title: Capital A considers divesting Big Pay, Tune Protect stake as it restructures Move Digital to address RM292mil liabilities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Capital A Bhd is undertaking a court-supervised scheme of arrangement for its wholly-owned indirect subsidiary Move Digital Sdn Bhd, which could see the divestment of the latter's stake in Big Pay Pte Ltd, and Tune Protect Group Bhd.
Move Digital is seeking an order to convene a meeting with its creditors and a three-month restraining order.
The company filed its application at the Kuala Lumpur High Court today (Sept 18), as it seeks to resolve historical liabilities, streamline corporate holdings and eliminate funding for loss-making units.
The filing immediately triggered an automatic two-month moratorium prohibiting winding-up proceedings, receivership appointments, or legal enforcement actions against Move Digital without court leave.
"This is about accountability, governance and taking control of our future," said Tan Sri Tony Fernandes, group CEO of Capital A said in a statement announcing the restructuring.
"We are cleaning up our legacy assets and focusing 100 per cent of our energy and capital on our high-growth businesses. This move makes our financial position stronger and allows us to double down on what we do best."
The primary sources of recovery include a potential market-driven divestment of all or a majority of Move Digital's 99.56 per cent equity interest in Big Pay.
The group is also exploring an orderly divestment of Move Digital's 13.6 per cent quoted equity stake in Tune Protect broadly in line with fair market value.
It is also looking at the systematic collection of related-party receivables, estimated at approximately RM32 million to RM32.2 million.
The scheme creditors involved are primarily internal group entities, including Capital A itself, AirAsia SEA Sdn Bhd, AirAsia Move, Ikhlas Com Travel Sdn Bhd, Santan Food Sdn Bhd, AirAsia Bhd, and PT Indonesia AirAsia.
Move Digital's financial distress stems from intercompany debt within the Capital A group alongside significant legal liabilities resulting from the arbitral award involving the minority shareholders of Big Pay.
On Dec 27, 2024, the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) required Move Digital to acquire the holdings of two minority shareholders in Big Pay for US$14.74 million, following the shareholder dispute that began in 2021.
A final award on costs issued on July 18, 2025 requiring Move Digital to pay US$4.13 million in legal fees, accruing interest at 5.33% per annum from Aug 9, 2025.
Capital A clarified that Move Digital is entirely separate and distinct from AirAsia Move Sdn Bhd, the group's digital travel platform and online travel agency, which is directly owned by Capital A. AirAsia Move continues its day-to-day operations without disruption.
Under the proposed framework, scheme creditors' claims will rank pari passu as unsecured obligations and will be settled through a three-year monetisation plan.
Move Digital operates solely as an investment holding vehicle and does not carry on any operational business.
According to its audited financial statements for the fiscal year ended Dec 31, 2025, the company reported a net liability position of approximately RM292 million and limited cash resources.
Capital A stated that the exercise is driven by disciplined capital allocation rather than group liquidity constraints, allowing the company to reallocate resources toward higher-return core operations.
Executing the scheme will enable Capital A to achieve the positive deconsolidation of BigPay's historical operating losses from its consolidated financial balance sheet.
The proposed scheme is not expected to have a material impact on Capital A's group structure, share capital, gearing, net assets per share, or earnings per share, as Move Digital's losses are already recognized in the group financial statements and BigPay was in a shareholders' deficit position as of Dec 31, 2025.
Final execution of the scheme remains subject to asset validations, creditor engagement, court sanction, and regulatory approvals in Malaysia and relevant foreign jurisdictions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire chair, becomes chairman emeritus
Article:
NEW YORK: Berkshire Hathaway said on Friday that Warren Buffett will step down as the conglomerate's chairman and will become its chairman emeritus, effective immediately.
Earlier this year, Buffett had stepped down as chief executive officer (CEO), handing the reins to longtime lieutenant Greg Abel.
"Father Time always wins. He has, however, been generous with me," Buffett, 96, wrote in a letter to shareholders.
The conglomerate named his son, Howard Buffett, a Berkshire director since 1993, as chairman.
"As Chairman Emeritus, Mr. Buffett will remain a member of the Board of Directors and will continue to offer his valued judgment and perspective," Berkshire said in a statement.
Buffett built Berkshire into an approximately US$1.03 trillion conglomerate with dozens of businesses, including Geico car insurance, the BNSF railroad, Berkshire Hathaway Energy, Dairy Queen ice cream, Fruit of the Loom underwear and Squishmallows plush toys.
"The culture Warren built and the values he championed will remain at the heart of Berkshire, and Howard will be their guardian," Abel said in a statement on Friday.
Buffett's influence has extended far beyond Berkshire, shaping generations of corporate leaders and investors with his emphasis on long-term thinking, disciplined capital allocation and straightforward management.
CEOs across Corporate America have looked to him as a sounding board on everything from acquisitions and succession to navigating periods of market turmoil, while his annual shareholder meetings became a gathering point for investors seeking insight into the broader business landscape.
Buffett first announced plans to step away from the conglomerate in May 2025, surprising shareholders and analysts despite his age. After decades at the helm, he had become synonymous with the company, making his succession one of the most closely watched in corporate America.
In August, Berkshire said it began reducing its enormous stockpile of cash in the second quarter, investing billions ​of dollars in stocks such as Alphabet and repurchasing billions of its own, as it reported higher-than-expected profit.
Its quarterly operating profit rose 16 per cent to US$12.98 ​billion, topping analyst forecasts, while net income more than doubled to US$25.67 billion, including unrealised gains and losses on stocks that Omaha, Nebraska-based Berkshire still owns.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 14 foreign motorists caught without valid licences within four hours
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Police seized 14 vehicles, including 11 motorcycles and three cars, during a four-hour special operation targeting foreign motorists here today.
The vehicles were seized after their foreign drivers and riders were found to be operating without valid driving licences.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the operation, conducted by the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division from 7am to 10am, also saw 39 traffic summonses issued for various offences.
He said all 14 vehicles were seized under Section 64 of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"The operation focused on foreign drivers and motorcyclists who failed to comply with traffic laws and regulations in the district.
"Among the main offences detected were 14 cases of driving without a valid licence under Section 26(1), eight cases involving motor vehicle licences or road tax under Section 23(1), and five cases of driving without insurance protection under Section 90(1)," he said in a statement.
He added that another 12 summonses were issued for various traffic offences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rauf: Melaka to keep cutting protocol to give public direct access to leaders
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh says his administration will continue to do away with protocol in engagements with the people so they have direct access to state leaders.
He said the approach allows leaders and officials to hear the people's concerns and complaints first-hand.
"We will not change this. Members of the public can approach anyone, visit any counter, meet their elected representatives or exco members, or even see the chief minister if they wish," he said after attending a meet-the-people session in Tanjung Bidara.
Rauf said the initiative aligns with the "Melaka Sayang Rakyat" policy, which aims to simplify administrative procedures and cut red tape.
He added that resolving issues raised by the people was vital to boosting confidence in the state government.
"If we resolve these complaints, we can achieve an approval rating of over 75 per cent from the people," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Mak Ton' found alone, covered in faeces at Ulu Tiram home
Article:
ULU TIRAM: An elderly woman was found lying on the floor, covered in faeces, inside a squalid home where the electricity and water supplies had been cut off for months.
The woman, known only as Mak Ton, was found inside her terrace house in Kampung Mawar here on Sept 12.
Neighbours of different races stepped in to help her, giving her a bath before arranging for an ambulance to take her to Sultan Ismail Hospital.
Kampung Oren and Tebrau village chairman Johar Samat said neighbours became concerned after she was not seen outside her house for several days.
"When they went to check, she was found lying on the living room floor, believed to have fallen, with her body covered in faeces.
"The house was also filled with rubbish and food waste, while the electricity and water supplies had been disconnected for several months," he said.
Mak Ton, who is believed to have Alzheimer's disease, had been living alone since her husband died. She had previously refused neighbours' attempts to visit her or help clean the house.
Her age could not be determined as no identification documents were found. She is currently being treated at the hospital for hypertension and diabetes.
Johar said the woman was a monthly aid recipient of the Johor Islamic Religious Council, which she usually used to buy food.
Residents later held a gotong-royong to clean the house and are now seeking help from the authorities to trace her relatives, who are believed to be living in Larkin and Penang.
"Do not let those who once raised us spend their final years in loneliness and neglect," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No sign of Najib's family at Langgak Duta residence as of 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: There was no sign of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's family members at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence as of 7pm today, hours after he was granted a conditional royal pardon.
Checks at the residence found that members of the media and Najib's supporters remained gathered outside, awaiting further developments following the announcement earlier today.
Najib is not expected to return to the residence today as several processes are understood to have to be completed before he can begin serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
](https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1535573/updated-najibs-special-officer-tight-lipped-media-wait-outside-jalan)
Earlier today, Najib's special officer
Ahmad Lutfi Azhar
was seen arriving at his Langgak Duta residence, hours after he was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
He was seen entering the compound in a black Proton sport utility vehicle (SUV) at about 4.35pm.
His arrival marked one of the first movements observed at the residence, where more than 50 local and international media personnel, as well as supporters, have been stationed since earlier today following the announcement of the conditional pardon.
Lutfi has remained tight-lipped on developments hours after the former prime minister was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
He emerged from Najib's residence in Jalan Langgak Duta to distribute water to more than 50 media personnel who had been waiting for hours for any sign of Najib or his wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor.
Asked how the family was doing and whether they would be coming to the house, Lutfi said he could not comment.
Asked whether the media should continue waiting outside the house, Lutfi said it was up to them.
Police patrols
were seen periodically making their rounds in the area.
Earlier today, the Federal Territories Pardons Board announced that Najib, 73, had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under
house arrest
until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
The decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya at Istana Negara today.
The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
Najib must comply with all conditions imposed under the pardon, failing which it will be revoked and he will be required to immediately serve the remainder of his sentence in prison.
Najib has been serving his sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction and sentence in the SRC International case.
He was convicted of seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million belonging to SRC International.
Najib was originally sentenced to 12 years' jail and fined RM210 million.
In 2024, the Pardons Board reduced his
jail term
to six years and his fine to RM50 million, setting his release date at Aug 23, 2028.

Title: YTL Power lines up 5.2 GW gas build, US firms among potential off-takers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: YTL Power International Bhd is planning more than 5.25 gigawatts (GW) of new gas-fired power generation capacity across Malaysia and Southeast Asia, a major expansion driven by surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres.
People familiar with the matter told Business Times that the planned projects, spanning Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam, could involve a total investment of more than RM42 billion.
The new capacity is expected to serve large-scale data centre and AI infrastructure developments, with major technology companies and US-based hyperscale data centre operators among potential power off-takers, the sources said.
Specific off-take agreements have yet to be disclosed.
The expansion could increase YTL Power's total installed generation capacity to more than 11GW by 2030.
This will significantly strengthen its regional power-generation footprint as the group simultaneously expands its data-centre and AI infrastructure businesses.
One source said the planned power expansion was closely linked to YTL Power's strategic relationship with Nvidia, which has backed the group's AI cloud ambitions.
"This is just the beginning. Nvidia is more than a partner with YTL Power. This expansion is part of the existing strategic partnership with Nvidia," the source said.
Nvidia executive vice-president and chief financial officer Colette Kress highlighted the emergence of regional AI infrastructure providers, including YTL AI Cloud in Malaysia, during the chipmaker's second-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call.
The sources said YTL Power was also evaluating additional opportunities across Asia as electricity demand from data centres, AI computing and other energy-intensive industries accelerates.
"Expanding the generation portfolio will give YTL Power greater control over a critical input for its data-centre operations, while positioning the group to supply electricity to other large-scale industrial and technology customers across Southeast Asia," one source said.
YTL Power shares have climbed nearly 67 per cent since the start of the year, reflecting growing investor interest in the group's exposure to the fast-expanding data centre and AI infrastructure market.
The stock rose as high as RM5.71 today before pairing gains and was at RM5.56 at 11.27am, valuing the company at about RM48.64 billion.
YTL Power has traded between RM2.51 and RM6.02 over the past 52 weeks, highlighting the strong re-rating of the utility and infrastructure group as demand for power and data centre capacity accelerates.
The group's planned investment underscores the growing convergence between Southeast Asia's data-centre boom and power infrastructure, as operators seek long-term access to reliable and competitively priced electricity.
AI workloads are particularly electricity-intensive, increasing pressure on data centre developers and technology companies to secure power supply alongside land, connectivity and computing capacity.
The expansion comes as YTL Power, Ganda Power and Siemens Energy signed reservation agreements on Sept 14 for four additional SGT-9000HL gas turbine units, taking the total number of turbines ordered under the arrangement to seven.
YTL Power managing director Datuk Seri Yeoh Seok Hong said recently the turbines would underpin new power projects in Malaysia and the wider region.
"Energy is the foundation of the AI economy," he said, adding that YTL Power was combining its power-generation expertise with its growing capabilities in data centres and AI infrastructure to support customers and emerging industries.
The turbine reservations also come amid a global supply squeeze for large gas turbines, with rising demand from data centres and other power-intensive industries contributing to extended delivery lead times.
YTL Power's power-generation expansion is aligned with its plan to double its data-centre capacity to 2.4GW by 2030.
The group currently operates a 300-megawatt data-centre campus in Kulai, Johor, backed by Nvidia, with expansion plans that could increase capacity to 1.2GW by 2030.
Separately, YTL's SIPP Power is developing another 1.2GW data-centre facility in Sedenak, Johor, further expanding the group's exposure to the region's rapidly growing data-centre market.

Title: Civil servant arrested after faking theft of wife's Vellfire for insurance payout
Article:

Title: Najib's house arrest could hurt Malaysia's anti-graft credibility — TI-M
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest could have serious implications for Malaysia's anti-corruption credibility, said Transparency International Malaysia (TI-M).
Its president, Dr Raymon Ram, said that while the organisation respected the constitutional power of clemency under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, Najib's conviction involving RM42mil had been unanimously upheld by the Federal Court.
"The concern goes beyond one individual. Exceptional treatment of a person convicted in a major corruption case risks reinforcing the perception that those with political influence or status may face different consequences from ordinary offenders.
"It may also set expectations for similar treatment in future cases involving grand corruption and financial crime, potentially weakening the deterrent effect of Malaysia's anti-corruption framework," he said in a statement.
He added that the case also had implications for Malaysia's international standing on the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) global ranking.
"High-profile decisions involving accountability for corruption inevitably contribute to the wider environment in which those perceptions are formed.
"Malaysia should be strengthening confidence in the integrity of its institutions, not creating further uncertainty over whether accountability is applied consistently.
"Malaysia's anti-corruption credibility will ultimately be judged by whether the principles of accountability, proportionality and equality before the law remain equally strong when those involved are powerful," he said.
Ram said the country's progress in strengthening governance and rebuilding institutional confidence must not be undermined by perceptions of preferential treatment in cases that have come to symbolise Malaysia's fight against grand corruption.
Earlier today,
the Federal Territories Pardons Board
said Najib had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case.
The board said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
It added that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed under the pardon, failing which the conditional pardon could be revoked.

Title: Perlis Umno launches solidarity fund for Najib
Article:

He said Perlis Umno conveyed its highest appreciation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia for granting the conditional pardon.
He also urged Malaysians to accept the decision with maturity and decorum, regardless of political differences.
"Those who are grateful, let them express their gratitude with decorum, while those who hold different views should do so respectfully. Let us not turn this decision into a platform to prolong disputes.
"Politics may differ and positions may vary, but we continue to uphold the Constitution and respect the institution of the Malay Rulers," he said.

Title: Stray dog-catcher probed over obscene gesture
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Police have recorded the statement of an animal management contractor stray dog-catcher over an alleged obscene and humiliating hand gesture towards a 29-year-old woman during an operation in Sri Gading here yesterday.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the woman lodged a report at 2.02am today, alleging that the incident occurred around 11.30am yesterday.
He said initial investigations found that the woman was passing through a housing area when she encountered several workers appointed by the local council to conduct the stray animal operation.
"A misunderstanding occurred between both parties, after which one of the dog-catcher allegedly made a hand gesture understood to be obscene and humiliating towards the complainant," he said in a statement.
Shahrulanuar said police were investigating the case under Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955, which covers the use of obscene, threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour.
"The person concerned has given a statement and the investigation papers will be referred immediately to the Johor deputy public prosecutor for further action," he said.

video of an alleged confrontation

Title: Evocom IPO draws 3.6 times oversubscription
Article:

Title: Perdana Putra abuzz ahead of PH Presidential Council meeting
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Perdana Putra complex here came under close media attention today as the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council was set to meet amid heightened political developments surrounding Barisan Nasional's (BN) position in the unity government.
Several vehicles believed to be carrying political leaders were seen entering the complex from about 5.20pm, with members of the media gathering outside the Prime Minister's Office from about 4pm ahead of the scheduled 5.30pm meeting.
The meeting, chaired by PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, is expected to discuss current political developments, including BN's position in the unity government.
The identities of those in the vehicles could not immediately be confirmed.
The meeting comes amid renewed political attention following the decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under conditional house arrest, subject to a RM50 million fine.
Najib was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
The decision has reignited political discussion within Umno, with analysts saying it could revive the "Bossku" sentiment among sections of the party's grassroots and increase pressure on Umno to be more vocal in defending its former president.
The PH meeting also follows remarks by BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at the 2026 Umno general assembly last week, when he challenged those calling for the party to end its cooperation with the unity government.
Zahid said those seeking to end the cooperation should either call for the dissolution of Parliament to pave the way for the 16th general election (GE16), or table a motion of no confidence against the government in the Dewan Rakyat.
His remarks have since fuelled renewed discussion over BN's position in the unity government and the future of the coalition.
On Monday, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke called on Anwar to convene the
PH Presidential Council
meeting immediately to discuss recent political developments.
Loke said the meeting should be held as soon as Anwar returned from his official overseas visit, citing several political statements made recently which he described as detrimental to political certainty and stability in the country.
Today's meeting is expected to give PH leaders an opportunity to discuss the latest developments and their implications for the coalition's relationship with BN.
The issue is particularly sensitive as BN remains a key component of the unity government, while the Najib decision has generated strong reactions within Umno and among its supporters.
The media remained gathered outside Perdana Putra as vehicles continued to arrive ahead of the meeting.
As of press time, no political leaders had emerged to speak to the media.

Title: Vestland secures RM107mil slope mitigation contract in Terengganu
